parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Traditional Māori fishing hooks
parts.article:
Maori Fish Hooks V2

(A) The discovery of ancient fishing hooks in New Zealand has revealed that the Māori people were remarkably skilled at crafting highly effective tools for catching fish. These hooks, often made from organic materials such as bone or shell, functioned with surprising precision, even when compared to modern alternatives. However, for many centuries, their true purpose was misunderstood by researchers and collectors alike. Many assumed these intricately shaped hooks served only decorative, ceremonial, or ritualistic purposes due to their unusual appearance and craftsmanship. Ironically, in recent years, engineers and product designers have turned to modern technologies – such as 3D scanning and computer-aided manufacturing – to recreate these hooks. These reproductions, now made using high-tech materials, replicate the original Māori designs that were created over a millennium ago.

(B) When the Māori first arrived in New Zealand from the Pacific Islands, they encountered an environment rich in natural resources. They quickly adapted by using familiar materials such as bones and stones to make their fishing hooks and began practicing intensive agriculture. Their fishing lines and nets, made from native plants like flax and cabbage trees, proved just as strong – if not stronger – than those used by Europeans, which were typically made from hemp. Although the structure of the Māori hooks was highly efficient for catching fish, their form was somewhat limited. This was because the materials they had access to could not be forged or bent like metal, thus restricting the range of shapes the hooks could take.

(C) More than 230 years after the Māori settled, Europeans landed in New Zealand and began exploring the land. As they moved through the region, they came across various local fishing tools, including the Māori hooks. Despite their effectiveness, many Europeans viewed the tools with skepticism. They considered them awkward and ineffective, failing to recognize the ingenuity of the designs. Even modern archaeologists sometimes share this view, finding the hooks odd and questioning their efficiency. In 1777, however, William Anderson made an observation that challenged this view. He noted that although the hooks looked unconventional, the Māori had already developed advanced methods of intensive farming – evidence of their broader ingenuity. Still, the unusual appearance of the hooks overshadowed how successful they truly were.

(D) Recent research conducted by Victoria University has revealed that Māori fishing hooks functioned quite differently from those used by Europeans. Rather than piercing directly like a standard hook, Māori hooks worked by rotating the fish away from the point and catching it securely under the jaw. This rotational mechanism proved remarkably effective in practice. Unlike the lever-based mechanisms common in European designs, the Māori hooks employed a unique principle that required neither barbs nor baiting in the same manner, showcasing a distinctly original approach to fishing.

(E) After the 1700s, Māori craftsmen began using new materials introduced by Europeans, such as metals. However, they did not abandon their traditional designs. Instead, they incorporated the new materials into the same forms they had long used. As bones and stones fell out of use, hooks made from traded metals became more common. Some artisans even used rare and valuable materials like ivory or greenstone, crafting hooks that were later taken into luxury markets and sold as jewelry, blurring the line between utility and art.

(F) Following the 1800s, Europe began exporting mass-produced hooks to New Zealand. These items were cheaper and quickly gained popularity among local users. Despite their affordability, the production of traditional Māori hooks declined due to the nails and other metallic materials required, which were difficult to manipulate without specialized tools. In the early 1900s, however, interest in Pacific culture grew, and collectors began to seek out original Māori fishing hooks once again. This renewed attention turned the hooks into coveted antique items. Unfortunately, the demand also led to a wave of imitations—many of the hooks appearing on the market today are fake, though they can usually be identified by their inconsistent design and materials.

(G) The Māori did not only adapt their fishing hooks through European influence but also modified other traditional items using both metals and more recently, synthetic plastic. Importantly, these changes were often adaptations rather than complete replacements, preserving core aspects of Māori design. What is perhaps most remarkable is that many hooks found on boats in New Zealand today still bear a striking resemblance to the ancient forms crafted hundreds of years ago, a testament to the enduring utility and brilliance of traditional Māori design.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到这些鱼钩的真正用途几个世纪以来都被研究人员和收藏家误解了，以为只是装饰或仪式用的。
你可能会忽略原文里的“misunderstood”（误解），这个词完美对应了题目里的“mistaken opinions”。

However, for many centuries, their true purpose was misunderstood by researchers and collectors alike. Many assumed these intricately shaped hooks served only decorative, ceremonial, or ritualistic purposes due to their unusual appearance and craftsmanship.

questions.question: Fishing is more difficult in New Zealand than Pacific islands.

analyses.content: 原文只提到了毛利人从太平洋岛屿来到新西兰时遇到了丰富的自然资源，根本没有比较在这两个地方钓鱼哪个更难。
你可能会因为看到这两个地名挨在一起，就根据常识强行脑补难度对比，记住原文没明说比较关系就是 Not Given。

questions.question: Māoris use new materials to build hooks after they arrived New Zealand.

analyses.content: 原文明说他们到达新西兰后，用的是“熟悉的”（familiar）材料来做鱼钩，这跟题目里说的“新的”（new）材料完全相反。
你可能会把他们到了“新”西兰（New Zealand）误以为他们用了“新”材料，做题时一定要死盯“familiar”这个词。

questions.question: Māoris’ hooks are limited in forms because of the material limitation it used.

analyses.content: 原文直接说明了毛利鱼钩的形状（form）受限，原因正是他们能用的材料无法像金属那样被锻造或弯曲。
这题很直白，你只要别把原文前半句的“structure”（结构高效）和“form”（形状受限）搞混就不会选错。

Although the structure of the Māori hooks was highly efficient for catching fish, their form was somewhat limited. This was because the materials they had access to could not be forged or bent like metal, thus restricting the range of shapes the hooks could take.

questions.question: The fishing line of Māoris is worse than the European.

analyses.content: 原文说毛利人的鱼线跟欧洲人的相比“一样结实甚至更结实”（just as strong – if not stronger），这和题目里的“更差”（worse）截然相反。
你可能会看漏“if not stronger”这个关键表达，它是用来强调毛利鱼线质量非常好的。
Their fishing lines and nets, made from native plants like flax and cabbage trees, proved just as strong – if not stronger – than those used by Europeans, which were typically made from hemp.

questions.question: Europeans are given fishing hooks as a gift from local Māoris.

analyses.content: 原文只说欧洲人探索时“偶然发现”（came across）了这些鱼钩，全篇根本没提到毛利人把鱼钩当作“礼物”（gift）送给他们。
你可能会主观臆断欧洲人手里的鱼钩是当地人送的，千万别给自己加戏，没写就是没写。

你可能会因为原文写的是“farming”而不是原原本本的“crop growing”而不敢选 TRUE，要学会识别这种简单的同义替换。

这道题属于送分题，你只要把“differently”和“same way”对上号就能秒杀。

analyses.content: 原文提到用珍贵材料制作的鱼钩后来被当作珠宝（jewelry）售卖，正好对应题目里问的有价值的鱼钩被做成了什么。
你可能会犹豫想填“art”或者“luxury”，但“sold as jewelry”给出了最具体的产品形式，是唯一正解。
Some artisans even used rare and valuable materials like ivory or greenstone, crafting hooks that were later taken into luxury markets and sold as jewelry, blurring the line between utility and art.
原文说明传统鱼钩产量下降的原因是制作需要用到钉子（nails）和其他金属材料，而这些材料很难操作。
你可能会直接在“metals”前面乱找词，注意看原文是“nails and other metallic materials”，顺理成章提取“nails”。
Despite their affordability, the production of traditional Māori hooks declined due to the nails and other metallic materials required, which were difficult to manipulate without specialized tools.
原文清晰地写着在1900年代早期，收藏家（collectors）开始“再次”（once again）寻找原版的毛利鱼钩，对应题目的“再次感兴趣”。
你如果句子结构没看清，可能会抓错主语，找准是谁发出了“seek out”这个动作就行了。
In the early 1900s, however, interest in Pacific culture grew, and collectors began to seek out original Māori fishing hooks once again.
原文指出今天市场上出现的许多鱼钩都是假的（fake），并且它们很容易通过不一致的设计被识别出来。
你可能会想填前面的“imitations”，虽然意思对，但是“fake”直接跟在“are”后面，语法和句意上最贴合题目的空缺。
Unfortunately, the demand also led to a wave of imitations—many of the hooks appearing on the market today are fake, though they can usually be identified by their inconsistent design and materials.
原文说今天在新西兰的船上（boats）发现的许多鱼钩，依然和几百年前的古老形态非常相似。
你可能会手快填“New Zealand”，但注意题目介词是“on”，后面接的地点载体是“boats”（在船上），而不是“在国家上”。

What is perhaps most remarkable is that many hooks found on boats in New Zealand today still bear a striking resemblance to the ancient forms crafted hundreds of years ago, a testament to the enduring utility and brilliance of traditional Māori design.
